diagnosis: HBV calibrated with DDS (5000 runs total, NSE objective) on 1971-10 to 1997-12 after a one-year warm-up. Initial stores were set near their long-term means (soil 270 mm, lower zone 40 mm). Daily NSE is 0.903, KGE 0.944, bias -2.3% and r 0.95, so the fit is strong for a responsive, steep, grass-covered catchment on fractured limestone and gritstone in the Peak District. Final parameters: FC ≈ 326 mm, LP ≈ 1.0 (at its upper limit), BETA ≈ 3.35, PERC ≈ 5.1 mm/d, K2 ≈ 0.038 (a large baseflow component from the fractured aquifer), K1 ≈ 0.165, K0 ≈ 0.92 with UZL ≈ 55 mm (rarely active) and MAXBAS ≈ 2.9 days. Snow matters little (3.6% of precipitation falls as snow), so the snow parameters, including CWH (stuck at its lower limit), are poorly identified but have little effect. A second DDS search with a different seed stopped at nearly the same parameters (NSE 0.9030 to 0.9032), so the optimum appears stable. I did not test on a separate held-out period. Likely weaknesses are the timing of the sharpest flood peaks, which the model underestimates (simulated maximum 11.0 vs observed 13.9 mm/d), and the shape of dry-summer recessions, which depend on the groundwater store. Overall confidence is moderate to high, and I expect an NSE of about 0.85 to 0.9 in 1998-2008.
